After the 2nd RIGHT, the green with white center shows W at (30,26),(31,25),(31,26),(32,26). That's 4 white pixels. Hmm, that looks like the white 2x2... no wait.
Ah, wait. I think I get it: the object is 3x3, but the white "center" pixel is at (31,25), and the W pixels at (30,26),(31,26),(32,26) are... part of the white 2x2 that was at columns 30-32? No, that's not it either.
Let me look at the image from the previous turn (after the 2nd RIGHT): the green square with white center is at approximately columns 24-26, and the white square is at columns 27-29? In the image, the green with white center is adjacent to the white square, and the green with black center is between them? Actually, the image shows: [green with white center][green with black center][white] — hmm, in the image after the 2nd RIGHT: green with white center at about columns 24-26, then green with black center at about columns 27-29? No wait, the image shows a small green with white center, then a small green with black center, then a white square, then the purple bar.
Hmm, but in the 2nd RIGHT diff, the green with black center is still at columns 27-29 (unchanged). And the white 2x2 is at columns 30-32 (unchanged). So the row 30 layout after the 2nd RIGHT: columns 24-26 = green with white center (with extra W?), columns 27-29 = green with black center, columns 30-32 = white.
But the diff says (30,26)='W'. That's the right column of the green with white center being white. Contradiction... unless the green with white center object is actually 4 wide? No, that's not it.
Hmm, wait. Let me re-verify: maybe the white center of the green with white center is 2x2: rows 30-31? No, in the initial state it was 1 pixel at (31,19).
Actually, let me recompute the 2nd RIGHT diff more carefully. The diff list:
(30,21,'N','w'), (30,22,'N','w'), (30,23,'N','w'), (30,24,'w','N'), (30,25,'w','N'), (30,26,'w','W'),
(31,21,'N','w'), (31,22,'W','w'), (31,23,'N','w'), (31,24,'w','N'), (31,25,'w','W'), (31,26,'w','W'),

Row 30: columns 24=N, 25=N, 26=N
Row 31: columns 24=N, 25=W, 26=N
Row 32: columns 24=N, 25=N, 26=N
Clean again. And the 3rd RIGHT diff: (30,26,'W','N'),(31,26,'W','N'),(32,26,'W','N') — the white right column became green. And (30,27-29) N→w, (31,27-29) N→w, (31,28) B→w — the green with black center disappeared from columns 27-29. And a new green with black center appeared at columns 42-44.
So what happened on the 3rd RIGHT: the green with white center stayed at columns 24-26 (only the extra white pixels turned green — as if the object "settled"), and the green with black center teleported from columns 27-29 to columns 42-44 (jumped over the purple bar to the right panel)!
Hmm, interesting. So maybe the mechanics are: the green with white center is the "player" that moves 3 cells per arrow press. When it's adjacent to / overlaps with the green with black center, pressing RIGHT causes the green with black center to "pass through" the purple bar and jump to the other side? That seems strange.
Another interpretation: the green with black center is a "ghost" that follows the player after a delay? Or the green with black center is a "token" that gets pushed: when the player (green with white center) touches it and moves in that direction, the token gets launched across the purple bar?
Wait, actually, let me reconsider. Maybe the green with white center is the player, and the green with black center is an "enemy" or "key". The white 2x2 at columns 27-29 (now 6 wide at columns 27-32) — after the green with black center left, the white region expanded to columns 27-32. So the white 2x2 "grew" to fill the space the green with black center vacated? Or the white 2x2 is actually a 2x4... let me check the current white region: row 30: columns 27-32 = 'wwwwww' (6 wide). Rows 30-32? Row 31: columns 27-32 = 'wwwwww'. Row 32: same. So a 3x6 white rectangle at rows 30-32, columns 27-32.
Hmm! So the white 2x2 (columns 30-32) + the space the green with black center vacated (columns 27-29) merged into a 3x6 white block. Maybe the white block is a "platform" or "bridge" that the player can stand on? Or the white block is a "gap" in the purple bar's row that the token can cross through?
Actually, maybe the mechanic is: the green with black center is a "ball" that rolls; the player (green with white center) pushes it; when pushed right, it rolls right, passes through the white block region, crosses the purple bar (the purple bar is a wall, but the ball passes through the white block row?), and lands at columns 42-44 on the right panel.
Hmm, the ball jumped from columns 27-29 to columns 42-44 — that's 15 columns, passing over the purple bar (columns 33-38). Maybe the ball "bounced" off the purple bar? Or the ball teleports to the other side when it hits the purple bar?
Let me think about the goal from another angle. Two frames: left frame at rows 32-36, columns 11-15; right frame at rows 26-30, columns 44-48. The green with black center is now at rows 30-32, columns 42-44, adjacent to the right frame (overlapping at column 44, row 30). Maybe the goal is to get the green with black center into the right frame! The frame is at rows 26-30, columns 44-48; the green with black center is at rows 30-32, columns 42-44. To fit it into the frame, it needs to move up 4 and right 2? The frame's white center is at rows 27-29, columns 45-47 (2x2). The green with black center is 3x3. Hmm, the frame is 4x4 with a 2x2 white center. The 3x3 green can't fit exactly into the 2x2 hole.
Maybe the goal is: the green with white center (player) needs to reach the frame? Or the white block needs to be moved?
Let me try: press UP and see what happens now (the player is at columns 24-26, rows 30-32; the green with black center is at columns 42-44, rows 30-32). Actually, first let me test whether the player can still move with LEFT/UP, and whether the green with black center follows.
Actually, let me reconsider the whole thing. Maybe the mechanic is: the arrow keys move the green with white center (the "cursor"/player) in 3-cell steps. The green with black center is a "ball" that gets pushed when the player moves into it (Sokoban-style). When the ball is pushed right and hits the purple wall... it teleported to the other side? That doesn't make sense in Sokoban.
Or: the green with black center is the player, and the green with white center is... no, the green with white center is the one that moved with RIGHT.
Wait, actually — maybe both moved! Let me re-verify: on the 3rd RIGHT, the green with white center was at columns 24-26 before, and is at columns 24-26 after? The diff shows no N movement at columns 24-25, only the W→N at column 26. So the green with white center didn't move (blocked by the green with black center at columns 27-29). And the green with black center moved 15 to the right.
Hmm, so when the player tried to move into the ball, the ball got launched? To where? Columns 42-44. What's at columns 42-44? The right panel, just to the left of the frame (frame at columns 44-48). The ball landed adjacent to the frame, overlapping at column 44, row 30.
Maybe the ball "bounced" off the purple bar: the ball at columns 27-29, pushed right, moves... passes through the white block (columns 30-32), hits the purple bar (columns 33-38), bounces back? No, it ended up on the other side at columns 42-44.
Or the ball teleports through the purple bar to the symmetric position on the other side: the purple bar is at columns 33-38 (center at column 35.5). The ball at columns 27-29 (center at column 28). Mirror across column 35.5: 35.5*2-28 = 43 → center at column 43, so columns 42-44. Yes! The ball mirrored across the purple bar's center! So the purple bar acts like a "mirror"/"portal": objects that hit it get mirrored to the other side.
So the mechanic: the player (green with white center) pushes the ball (green with black center); the ball slides in that direction until it hits the purple bar, and gets mirrored to the other side.
Now the goal: probably to get the ball into the frame on the right panel (the frame is a "hole"/goal). The ball is now at rows 30-32, columns 42-44. The right frame is at rows 26-30, columns 44-48. To get the ball into the frame, push it up? If I push the ball up, it slides up... what stops it? The top edge of the panel is at row 21. The frame is at rows 26-30. Hmm, if the ball slides up from rows 30-32, it would go to rows 21-23 (top edge), not into the frame.
Or the goal is to get the ball into the left frame? The left frame is at rows 32-36, columns 11-15.
Or the goal is to get the player (green with white center) into a frame?
Hmm. Let me think about what "solving" looks like. Maybe: get the ball into one of the frames (the white center of the frame = the goal hole). The ball is 3x3, the frame's hole is 2x2. The ball's black center pixel could fit into the hole.
The ball is currently at rows 30-32, columns 42-44; the right frame's hole is at rows 27-29, columns 45-47. To align the ball's center (31,43) with the hole's center (28,46): move up 3, right 3.
How does the ball move? The player pushes it. The player is at columns 24-26, rows 30-32. The ball is at columns 42-44, rows 30-32. The player can't push the ball directly (too far). But the player can move around (3-cell steps) and push the ball from the left, right, above, or below.
To push the ball up: the player needs to be below the ball (rows 33-35, columns 42-44) and press UP. The player moves in 3-cell steps; can it reach rows 33-35, columns 42-44? The player is currently at rows 30-32, columns 24-26. To get to the right panel, the player has to cross the purple bar (columns 33-38) — a wall. Can the player cross? Maybe the player also gets mirrored when it hits the purple bar!
Let me test: move the player right until it hits the purple bar and see if it mirrors. The player is at columns 24-26; the white block is at columns 27-32; the purple bar is at columns 33-38. Press RIGHT: the player moves to columns 27-29 (over the white block), then columns 30-32, then columns 33-35 → hits the purple bar → maybe mirrors to columns 36-38? Mirror of center at column 31 across 35.5: 40 → columns 39-41? Hmm, depends on the exact rule.
Actually wait — the ball was at columns 27-29 (center at column 28) and mirrored to columns 42-44 (center at column 43). 28 + 43 = 71 = 2*35.5. Yes, mirrored across the purple bar's centerline (column 35.5).
If the player at columns 24-26 (center at column 25) hits the bar: mirror center = 71-25 = 46 → columns 45-47. That's exactly where the right frame's hole is (columns 45-47)! Interesting, but the player's row would still be 30-32, and the frame is at rows 26-30.
I'm getting too deep into speculation. Let me probe systematically:
1. Press RIGHT (player at columns 24-26, path to the bar is clear: white block at columns 27-32). See if the player moves to columns 27-29 or mirrors.

sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
r = action(['RIGHT'])
b = previous_frame.ascii.split('\n')
c = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
diffs = [(rr, cc, b[rr][cc], c[rr][cc]) for rr in range(64) for cc in range(64) if b[rr][cc] != c[rr][cc]]
print(len(diffs), diffs)
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
